title: Unified Event Correlation Layer for Inference KPIs
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Problem:
We currently emit multiple siloed telemetry streams for inference requests: Prometheus counters/gauges for aggregated KPIs, OTel spans/traces for latency and request flow, and an event bus for sampled detailed request payloads. Correlating a single inference request from Prometheus metrics back to the sampled spans or the event payloads is brittle and expensive due to inconsistent IDs, high-cardinality tags (model+variant+input_hash), and variance in sampling. This makes root-cause analysis and regression detection across model rollouts slow and error-prone.

Goal:
Implement a lightweight, centralized correlation layer (Event Correlation Layer - ECL) that stitches per-request Prometheus/OTel telemetry and sampled event payloads into a queryable correlation key. The ECL should: (1) produce a compact correlation_id for high-volume requests, (2) enrich sampled spans/events with deterministic sampling metadata, (3) normalize a small, low-cardinality set of KPI labels for PrometheusEXposition, and (4) expose a look-up API to map correlation_id -> trace id / event pointer for investigation.

Design notes / proposal:
- Correlation key generation: compute a stable 128-bit fingerprint (hex) based on: service, model_name, model_version_hash, request_bucket (coarse hash of input length/type), and a timestamp bucket (1s). This keeps cardinality bounded while still separating hot keys across models/versions.
- Deterministic sampling metadata: attach a sampling_token (short base62) to a deterministic sampler (e.g., first N per-second per-model seeds) so sampled events can be reproduced across services. Sampling decisions are included in OTel span attributes and in a tiny Prometheus label sample_token when exported (only on sampled observations).
- Metric normalization layer: implement a middleware that converts high-cardinality tags (prompt_hash, user_id) into either label fingerprints or drops them for Prometheus metrics while emitting them into the event bus for later offline joins. The normalized label set for export will be: {model_family, model_variant, seq_bucket, offer_tier}.
- Lightweight lookup store: use an LRU-backed Redis cluster (TTL 5m) that maps correlation_id -> {trace_id, event_topic:offset, sample_token}. Expose a read-only /internal/observability/lookup/{correlation_id} endpoint with strict auth for console and SRE queries.
- Ingress/egress implementations: add middleware to inference-serving runtime to attach correlation_id to response metadata headers and to include it as a Prometheus exemplar when emitting latency histograms (via OpenMetrics exemplar support). For OTel traces, include correlation_id as span attribute 'redwood.correlation_id'.
- Rollout plan: start with shadow-mode enrichment on canary machines that only write to lookup store and to sampled events; after verifying traffic and cardinality, flip exemplar and response header writes in a staged rollout (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Trade-offs considered:
- Full fidelity IDs (request UUIDs) provide perfect correlation but blow up label cardinality and storage. We choose a bounded fingerprint to keep Prometheus and downstream storage practical.
- Using Redis for lookup provides operational simplicity and low-latency lookups; downside is an extra dependency to monitor under load. Consider a sharded in-cluster cache as Phase 2.

Operational concerns:
- Need SLOs for lookup endpoint (p99 < 50ms) and Redis eviction metrics alerts.
- Cost modeling required for extra Redis writes and increased event bus volume for sampled payloads.
- Security: correlation metadata should not include PII; ensure input hashes are irreversible and that sampling excludes customer-sensitive payloads unless explicit opt-in is provided.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic correlation_id is generated for >99% of inference requests in canary and present as 'redwood-correlation-id' response header.
OTel spans include 'redwood.correlation_id' attribute for traced requests and Prometheus histograms include exemplars with the same correlation_id when sampled.
Lookup API returns trace_id and event pointer for correlation_ids within TTL with 99th percentile < 50ms in canary.
A dashboard in Console shows correlation_id signing rate, unique key cardinality per model, and Redis hit/miss rates for the lookup store.
Documentation describing deterministic sampling algorithm, label normalization rules, and console usage published and linked from the ticket.
Security review completed: no PII escapes into Prometheus labels or correlation store; opt-out controls documented.

notes: Next steps: run a 30m canary with correlation writes disabled for Prometheus exemplars, validate key cardinality and Redis sizing, then schedule a controlled exemplar flip with on-call present. Reach out to Compliance for quick review on input hashing scheme.
attachments_summary: RFC + proto PR + initial benchmarking images
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: prototyping (generate correlation_id, write to Redis, attach span attribute)
Phase 2: shadow writes for exemplars and headers
Phase 3: staged rollout with dashboards and alerting
Phase 4: iterate on key fingerprinting and consider in-cluster cache
observability_metrics_to_track: correlation_write_qps, correlation_lookup_latency_p50/p95/p99, correlation_key_cardinality_by_model, redis_evictions_per_min, exemplar_emit_rate, sampled_event_volume
